pages.text: An old wooden boat lay upside down on the beach. There was shade underneath.
They wanted to turn it into their hideout. "This is our house!"
Lolo began carrying things over. Riri measured the space first. "The more, the better." "Things need proper places."
Lolo brought a blanket, a box, and a net. Three buckets came too.
The hideout filled with things. There was no room to get in.
Riri arranged the things in a row, from biggest to smallest.
The row grew long and stretched outside the hideout. Riri had nowhere to sit either.
They folded their arms and looked at each other. Just then, the cat slipped under the boat.
The cat settled in the middle of the blanket. They pushed things aside and squeezed in beside it.
All three sat shoulder to shoulder. It was cramped but strangely warm. The two rested their heads on each other's shoulders.
